# Marcus Aurelius quote sources

9 passages attributed to Marcus Aurelius in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Aurelius.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Marcus Aurelius

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Koine Greek

Cited here from

The Meditations, cited by book and section.

How to cite it

Book and section — Meditations VI.54 — because the numbering is stable and the individual sections are short. Name the translator: the Greek is compressed and the English renderings differ markedly.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

The Meditations is a private notebook, written to himself and never prepared for publication; the Greek title means “to himself.” Treating its entries as considered doctrines on offer to a reader misses what they are. Several entries also restate Epictetus, so a thought can be Marcus' paraphrase of another Stoic without any quotation marks.

2 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Marcus Aurelius?

Book and section — Meditations VI.54 — because the numbering is stable and the individual sections are short. Name the translator: the Greek is compressed and the English renderings differ markedly. This archive cites Marcus Aurelius from The Meditations, cited by book and section. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Marcus Aurelius?

The Meditations is a private notebook, written to himself and never prepared for publication; the Greek title means “to himself.” Treating its entries as considered doctrines on offer to a reader misses what they are. Several entries also restate Epictetus, so a thought can be Marcus' paraphrase of another Stoic without any quotation marks.

### What language did Marcus Aurelius write in?

Koine Greek. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
